title: Run both test suites in CI on a Windows runner - blocked on the @cubric/connector file: dependency
description:
MPI-443 made npm test + npm run test:desktop a release gate, but the gate is a human step in mpi-version-bump - nothing runs the suites on push. A windows-latest runner can run BOTH today: Electron needs no xvfb on Windows, and Playwright drives it through the electron npm binary, so no npx playwright install step is needed. The one blocker is real and must be decided first: package.json line 28 pins "@cubric/connector": "file:../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector", a sibling path that does not exist on a lone checkout, so npm ci fails before any test runs. Three ways out, all needing a call from the user: (a) a second actions/checkout of the private MadPonyInteractive/Cubric-Studio repo with a PAT secret, (b) publish @cubric/connector to a registry, (c) vendor it into this repo. Note the existing .github/workflows/build-portable.yml runs NO tests - it only dispatches the private mpi-ci build on a v* tag, so a red suite currently cannot stop a build.

FINDING 2026-08-04, and it changes the answer - do NOT vendor. Two of the three original options are worse than they looked, and there is a fourth that is better than all of them.

(a) private checkout is NOT enough on its own: packages/connector/dist is NOT tracked in Cubric-Studio (git ls-files returns 0 files for it). The repo ships TypeScript source only, so CI would have to check out the sibling, npm install inside it and run tsc before Vision npm ci could resolve the file: path. That is a second toolchain in the test job.

(c) vendoring inverts the documented ownership split - Cubric-Studio owns @cubric/connector and the broker, Vision is a consumer. A vendored copy of an INTEROP CONTRACT is the one kind of copy that must never drift, and nothing would tell us when it had.

(d) THE RECOMMENDED ONE: stop requiring it. All three consumers already load it with a dynamic import inside try/catch and are written to work without it - services/brokerBoot.js:61 literally reads `catch { return null; // SDK not installed in this build. }`, and server.js:146 and services/connectorResponder.js do the same. It is an OPTIONAL SDK declared as a hard dependency. Moving it out of `dependencies` (to optionalDependencies, or dropping it and relying on the sibling being present in dev) makes npm ci succeed on a lone checkout with no secret, no registry and no copy - and it very likely also fixes the SHIPPED macOS bug in MPI-416 (absorbed MPI-417): the file: dependency makes the macOS artifact ship a dangling @cubric/connector symlink, so our own documented xattr command errors for every Mac user.

MUST VERIFY BEFORE COMMITTING TO (d): that `npm ci` really tolerates an optionalDependencies file: path whose target is absent - optional deps are forgiven when their BUILD fails, and a missing file: target may still fail lockfile resolution. Test it on a COPY of the repo, not in place. Also confirm the connector still resolves for local dev when Cubric-Studio IS present, and re-check the macOS symlink claim against the build script rather than assuming it follows.
acceptance: Option (d) tested on a COPY of the repo first: with @cubric/connector moved out of dependencies, npm ci completes on a checkout with no Cubric-Studio sibling present
Local dev still works when the sibling IS present - the connector resolves and brokerBoot does not silently fall into its SDK-not-installed branch on a machine that has it
Whether this also fixes the macOS dangling-symlink half of MPI-416 is checked against the build script and recorded on that card either way
A .github/workflows/tests.yml runs npm test and npm run test:desktop on windows-latest, on push and pull_request to master plus workflow_dispatch
Playwright artifacts (test-results/) upload on failure so a red desktop run is diagnosable without reproducing locally
A red suite is proven to fail the workflow - verified by pushing a branch with a deliberately broken assertion, not assumed
Decided and written down whether a red suite should also block the v* tag build in build-portable.yml, which today dispatches with no tests at all
